data.name: Octbuster: Video Rental Store Cleanup
data.detailed_description:
Octbuster is a cozy organization game about closing up an 80s video rental store after hours as an octopus. With the help of your kitten pals, scoop up piles of procedurally placed VHS tapes with real tentacle arms and sort over 10,000 of them however you want. No timer, no score, no way to lose. Just you, nostalgia, and a store that slowly comes back together. 

Don't worry, you have 8 arms, a cart buddy, and an army of kittens.

There are over 10,000 tapes on the floor of this shop. Grabbing them one at a time would take forever, so you don't. Each tentacle is a real arm you aim and reach with, so you can scoop a whole pile at once, dump it in your cart, and slide tapes home while the shelf shuffles over to make room. Once you get in the rhythm it's super satisfying. 

The kittens help pick up tapes, hang around on the props you place, and dance to your music!

There is the one grumpy kitten... they mostly just knock over stuff and give you mean looks, but maybe they'll warm up to you as you get this placed cleaned up.

Every cover is procedurally generated. No generative AI.

There are 600 unique movies across 16 genres, all made using procedural generation and open-source word banks. This mattered to me enough that I built the whole pipeline from scratch, and it is included in-game as a custom movie-maker where you can generate or create your own movie titles to be used in the game.

No two shops are the same

Every new game scatters the shop fresh from a seed, so the pile is different every time. And if you want to mess with it, there are controls for how the tapes spawn, so you can do huge clumps or completely scattered.

Made so anyone can play it

Accessibility by design. Genres are told apart by shape and brightness, not just color, so the game stays readable for every kind of color vision. You can tune the size and font of the text, and every single sound has its own volume slider, so turn the plops way up and the music way down, whatever your ears want. There are comfort options for motion and screen effects too.

And then there's all this

  • A full upgrade system. Earn more arms, hold more tapes per arm, a bigger cart, and cart-specific upgrades too.

  • A wall of every movie you find. Hidden in the piles are one-of-a-kind display copies. Pick one up and it lights up and flies to the wall, filling in your collection one rare find at a time.

    • There are 600 to find. No rush, they turn up while you tidy.

  • Collectibles tucked under the mess, including cassette tapes that add to the shop's soundtrack and placeable props.

  • Make your own tapes. There's a full in-game maker for building your own movie covers, and Steam Workshop support is already in, so you can share them and stock your shelves with the community's stuff.

  • Play your own music through the shop and watch the lights sync to it.

  • Little minigames to find and play while you tidy.

  • Steam achievements that print into posters you can hang on the walls, stamped with your own stats from the run.

  • Speed-run modes with a built-in split timer and separate Any% and 100% categories.

  • Your own cozy corner to decorate, with the ability to free-place all your collectables that you've earned.

  • Collectables and decorations are all account bound, so new stores start with all the carefully placed decorations of the last one.

I'm also working on Simplified Chinese for launch. Chinese covers are regenerated from Chinese word banks and profanity filters, so I am considering paying a service for all the other player facing text.

Have fun!

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit (21H2+)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB / AMD RX 580 8GB (Shader Model 5.0)
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 6 GB available space
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 11 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-11400 / AMD Ryzen 5 5600
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA RTX 3060 / AMD RX 6600 8GB
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 6 GB available space

mac_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: macOS 13 Ventura
  • Processor: Apple M1 (Apple Silicon required)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Integrated Apple GPU (Metal 3)
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
mac_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: macOS 15 Sequoia or later
  • Processor: Apple M-series Pro or better
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Integrated Apple GPU, 16-core or better
  • Storage: 4 GB available space

linux_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS / SteamOS 3.5 (glibc 2.35+)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Vulkan 1.2 required — NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB (driver 535+) / AMD RX 580 8GB (Mesa 22.0+ RADV)
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: X11 or Wayland. Driver version matters more than GPU model on Linux.
linux_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS / SteamOS 3.6 or later
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-11400 / AMD Ryzen 5 5600
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA RTX 3070 (driver 550+) / AMD RX 6600 8GB (Mesa 24+)
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Upscaling is STP; DLSS and FSR 2 are not available on Linux.
